explanation: Socrates wrote nothing himself. Almost everything we know of his ideas comes from his students, above all Plato, whose dialogues often make him the main speaker.

claims.text: Socrates was sentenced to death in Athens in 399 BC and died by drinking hemlock.
Plato, Aristotle and Pythagoras were not executed with hemlock in Athens.
Socrates left no writings of his own.
Most of what is known of Socrates's ideas is found in the works of his students, especially Plato, whose dialogues often feature him as the main speaker.
